title: A Letter That Was Never Sent
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の史料、調査、システムの実証結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A local history club receives a box containing copies of old letters.
sentences.ja: 地域の歴史クラブは古い手紙の複製が入った箱を受け取る。

sentences.en: One letter describes a disagreement between several residents about the use of a public building.
sentences.ja: 一通は公共建物の利用について数人の住民の意見の相違を記述する。

sentences.en: The writer appears to ask an official to consider a different plan.
sentences.ja: 書き手は職員に別計画を検討するよう求めているように見える。

sentences.en: A student initially assumes that the letter was received by the official many years ago.
sentences.ja: 一人の生徒は当初、手紙が何年も前に職員に受け取られたと思う。

sentences.en: Another member of the club notices several corrections in the copied text.
sentences.ja: 別のクラブ員は複製本文の複数の訂正に気づく。

sentences.en: The letter also lacks information about the date on which it was sent.
sentences.ja: 手紙には送られた日付の情報もない。

sentences.en: The students begin to wonder whether the document might be an early version of a letter rather than a copy of a message that was actually delivered.
sentences.ja: 文書は実際に届けられた連絡の複製でなく手紙の初期版かもしれないと疑問に思い始める。

sentences.en: They recognize that the two possibilities would support different conclusions about the events.
sentences.ja: 二つの可能性は出来事について異なる結論を支えると認識する。

sentences.en: The students search for related documents that might provide further information.
sentences.ja: 追加情報を提供するかもしれない関連文書を探す。

sentences.en: A second document describes a meeting during which several residents discussed the same issue.
sentences.ja: 第二の文書は数人の住民が同じ問題を議論した会合を記述する。

sentences.en: It does not establish whether the official had received the particular letter.
sentences.ja: それは職員がその手紙を受け取ったか確定しない。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, it helps the students understand some of the concerns that existed at the time.
sentences.ja: それでも当時存在した懸念の一部を理解する助けになる。

sentences.en: Their club prepares a small exhibition presenting the two documents together.
sentences.ja: クラブは二文書を一緒に提示する小展示を準備する。

sentences.en: The description explains what each document reveals and which questions remain unanswered.
sentences.ja: 説明は各文書が明らかにすることと未解決の問いを述べる。

sentences.en: The students avoid describing the letter as evidence of the official's response to the residents.
sentences.ja: 手紙を住民への職員の対応の証拠として説明することを避ける。

sentences.en: They instead present it as evidence of a concern that someone considered expressing.
sentences.ja: 代わりに誰かが表明を考えた懸念の証拠として示す。

sentences.en: Historical documents can provide valuable information without answering every question about the events they describe.
sentences.ja: 歴史文書は記述する出来事の全質問に答えずとも価値ある情報を提供し得る。

sentences.en: A letter may reveal what someone intended to communicate without revealing whether the communication actually took place.
sentences.ja: 手紙は意思疎通が実際に起きたかを明らかにせず、誰かが何を伝えようとしたかを示し得る。

sentences.en: Readers should consider the history of a document as well as its contents.
sentences.ja: 読者は内容だけでなく文書の来歴も考慮すべきだ。

sentences.en: The unsent letter can still have a place in the history of a community.
sentences.ja: 送られなかった手紙も地域の歴史に位置づけを持ち得る。

vocabulary.definition: does not have enough of something

options: The construction of a new school.
A disagreement about a public building.
questions.explanation_ja: 公共建物利用に関する意見の相違。

questions.prompt: What does the student assume initially?
options: The official received the letter in the past.
The building no longer existed at the time.
Corrections and missing information about the sending date.
A description of the official's decision.

questions.prompt: Why does the distinction between a draft and a delivered letter matter?
options: Each supports different conclusions about what happened.
Every draft has necessarily been delivered.
All letters prove the recipient's response.
A draft cannot describe a concern.
questions.explanation_ja: 証明できる事柄が異なる。

questions.prompt: What does the second document describe?
options: The date of the first exhibition.
A meeting about the same issue.

questions.prompt: What can the second record help establish?
options: That the official definitely received the letter.
That certain concerns were discussed at the time.
That every resident agreed with the writer.
That the letter's author was the official.
What each document reveals and what remains uncertain.
Only a final date for every event.
The official's response as a confirmed fact.
The price of each original letter.

questions.prompt: Why avoid describing the letter as evidence of a response?
options: The letter gives a complete account of the response.
The students have confirmed no one discussed the issue.
It does not establish that the official received or acted on it.
Every written letter establishes that communication occurred.
Unsent texts are never historically useful.
An old document answers every historical question.
Historical documents must be interpreted in light of how they were created and used.
